story.title: Card freeze/unfreeze in mobile app with step-up authentication
story.description: Add card freeze/unfreeze controls to the mobile app through a new API gateway endpoint backed by card-service. Each card status change requires step-up authentication from authentication-service, binds the proof to the device and requested action, and exposes only masked card details. Update mobile-banking and api-gateway authorization policies together with the card control flow. PCI DSS review and security sign-off are outstanding: the prototype permits cross-device proof replay and lacks fail-closed verification evidence. These unresolved authentication defects and the missing rollback rehearsal are release blockers until the acceptance criteria have demonstrated evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A cardholder can freeze or unfreeze their own card in mobile-banking through the API gateway endpoint, and the refreshed view shows the confirmed status.
Each action requires a fresh step-up proof bound to the card, device and requested action; replay and cross-customer requests are rejected.
If authentication-service is unavailable or proof validation fails, card-service leaves the card status unchanged and denies the action.
Card control traces contain masked identifiers only; PCI DSS review, security sign-off and a rehearsed rollback are mandatory before release.

requirement.business_summary: Adds card freeze/unfreeze functionality to the mobile banking app, requiring step-up authentication and exposing only masked card details via a new API gateway endpoint backed by the card service.
requirement.technical_summary: Introduces a new REST endpoint in the API gateway that calls the card-service to update card status; each request mandates fresh step-up authentication from the authentication-service bound to device, card and action; mobile-banking UI and gateway authorization policies are updated to invoke the endpoint; responses return masked card identifiers only; card-service retains current status on auth failure or unavailability.
requirement.engineering_scope: Implement new API gateway endpoint for card freeze/unfreeze, integrate with card-service to update card status, add step-up authentication flow with authentication-service binding proof to device, card and action, update mobile-banking UI and API gateway authorization policies, ensure only masked card data is exposed, complete PCI DSS review and security sign-off, and rehearse rollback procedures.

tests.title: Security: Card freeze/unfreeze triggers audit event with masked card ID in audit-db
steps: Authenticate user in mobile banking app with valid device session.
Initiate step-up authentication for card freeze action (provide OTP or biometric).
Submit freeze request via mobile app to API gateway endpoint PATCH /mobile/cards/{id}/status with status frozen.
Verify step-up proof is validated by authentication-service.
Confirm card-service updates card status to frozen.
Check audit-db for an audit event corresponding to the freeze action.
Validate that audit event includes user ID, timestamp, action type, and masked card identifier (last four digits or token) but not full PAN.
tests.expected: Audit-db contains a newly created audit event with correct fields, masked card identifier present, full PAN absent.

tests.title: Compliance: Card freeze/unfreeze notification contains only masked card details via notification-service
steps: Perform card unfreeze via mobile app with valid step-up auth.
Capture outgoing notification triggered by notification-service (e.g., via mock or log).
Inspect notification payload (SMS, push, email) for card identifier.
Ensure payload displays only masked card number (e.g., ****1234) and not full PAN.
Verify that notification includes action description (unfreeze) and timestamp.
tests.expected: Notification sent, contains masked card identifier only, no full PAN.

tests.title: Operational: Risk engine logs and scores rapid card freeze/unfreeze attempts
steps: Authenticate user and complete step-up.
Rapidly send 5 freeze/unfreeze requests within 10 seconds using valid step-up proofs each time.
For each request, ensure authentication-service validates fresh step-up proof.
After sequence, query risk-engine for risk indicators or logs related to card ID.
Confirm risk-engine records elevated velocity score or flags unusual activity.
Verify that risk-engine response stays within defined thresholds and does not cause denial of service.
tests.expected: Risk engine logs show increased velocity metric for the card, and risk score remains within operational limits; no system errors.

tests.title: Security: ATM rejects transaction when card is frozen via mobile app
steps: Freeze a card using mobile app with valid step-up authentication.
Attempt to perform a withdrawal or balance inquiry at an ATM using the same card.
ATM forwards request to authorization (via api-gateway; assumes ATM checks card status via card-service).
Observe ATM response.
tests.expected: ATM declines transaction, displays error indicating card is blocked/frozen, and logs show card status fetched from card-service as frozen.

tests.title: Compliance: Branch portal API returns masked card identifier only for card status queries
steps: Authenticate a branch staff member with appropriate entitlement via authentication-service.

tests.expected: Successful response contains masked card identifier only; unauthorized request returns 403.

tests.summary: Selected 15 catalog tests and 8 new tests, covering 18 of 21 impacted nodes (86%); estimated effort is 13.2 hours.

frameworks.reason: PII-bearing components are impacted; the change touches customer data.

findings.text: The new card freeze/unfreeze capability routes customer- and account-linked requests through the mobile channel, the external gateway and an identity step-up challenge, so personal data processing exposure extends across the mobile banking surface, gateway routing layer, authentication service and card service as a result of this change.

Although responses are described as returning masked card identifiers only, the device-, card- and action-bound step-up proof introduces additional authentication and device-identifying artefacts whose minimisation, purpose limitation and retention characteristics require assessment alongside existing identity data held for the authentication service and card service.

Indirect exposure may reach customer profile, contact preference and notification components if card status changes trigger servicing updates or customer messaging through gateway-routed calls, warranting checks that the change does not widen the data reaching the customer service, customer database, CRM or notification service beyond their existing declared purposes.

recommendations: Assess and document data minimisation, purpose and retention for the personal data and step-up authentication artefacts handled by mobile-banking, api-gateway, authentication-service and card-service, and confirm the records of processing reflect the new card status journey.

Verify that subject rights handling, including access and erasure propagation, continues to function for the profile and contact data held in customer-service, customer-db, crm and notification-service when card status changes are processed through api-gateway.

Confirm that masked-only responses and logging practices on api-gateway, card-service and mobile-banking prevent exposure of full identifiers in payloads, traces and error paths, and evidence the checks in the change record.
Run privacy regression checks covering the new step-up path on authentication-service and the mobile-banking card status screen before release, including failure and unavailability scenarios.

frameworks.reason: card-data components are impacted; the change touches card data.

findings.text: The change introduces a card status update path reachable from the mobile channel through the external gateway to the card service, so checks are required that responses and downstream handling expose only masked card identifiers and that no sensitive card data is introduced into request, response or tracing flows.

Modification of the authentication flow to require fresh step-up proof bound to device, card and action raises exposure around token issuance, scope validation and privileged action authorisation, requiring review of the authentication service and gateway policy enforcement points.

Because the change touches card-related components, the controls around card data encryption, masking and role-based access restrictions warrant re-verification across the card service, gateway, identity layer, ATM channel and fraud screening components that interact with card activity.

recommendations: Verify card data encryption, masking and access restrictions remain effective for card-service, api-gateway, authentication-service, atm, fraud-engine and mobile-banking following the new endpoint and step-up flow.
Confirm that no sensitive authentication data is stored or logged by the new step-up path across authentication-service and api-gateway, and evidence the review of token and challenge handling.

Run card-data security testing and external API contract testing against api-gateway, card-service and mobile-banking, including rejection paths where step-up proof is absent, expired or bound to a different device or card.
Confirm monitored logging and alerting for card status changes remains in place on card-service, api-gateway and fraud-engine, and record the review evidence.

frameworks.reason: financial-data components are impacted; audit-data components are impacted.

findings.text: The change is scoped as a card servicing feature rather than a financial posting change, but the new gateway-routed action and its audit capture raise exposure around whether card status events create records with financial reporting or control relevance, which should be assessed for the gateway, card service and audit store.

Audit completeness for card freeze/unfreeze actions delivered through the mobile channel and gateway requires verification that append-only, integrity-checked events are captured for successful, failed and step-up-rejected attempts in the audit database.

If the updated gateway authorization policies or status changes reach account, ledger or payment components through existing routing, additional change-management and control-owner evidence may be needed beyond the directly changed components.

recommendations: Confirm with control owners whether card status changes introduced via api-gateway, card-service and mobile-banking generate financially relevant records, and document the conclusion and supporting rationale.

Verify that audit-db captures complete, immutable and attributable events for the new card status actions, including authentication failures and card-service unavailability, and retain the verification evidence.
Check that any indirect effect on account-service, transaction-db and payment-service routing is covered by change approval and testing evidence before release.
Record control-owner approval and evidence for schema, configuration or authorization policy changes applied to api-gateway, card-service and audit-db.

frameworks.reason: directly changed components have criticality >= 8; the authentication flow changes.

findings.text: The change directly modifies highly critical, tier-one components spanning the external gateway, identity provider, card platform and mobile channel, so service-owner approval, rollback planning and change-record evidence are expected for these components.

Adding a new external-facing endpoint constitutes an API contract change, requiring review of versioning, documentation, consumer communication and gateway policy configuration for the gateway and mobile channel.

The authentication flow and authorization policy changes need evidence of authorization testing and operational monitoring, including the stated fail-safe behaviour where the card service retains current status on authentication failure or unavailability.

recommendations: Obtain and record service-owner approval and a rehearsed rollback plan for api-gateway, authentication-service, card-service and mobile-banking before release.
Verify authorization and negative-path tests, including step-up rejection and fail-safe retention of card status, for api-gateway, authentication-service, card-service and mobile-banking.
Confirm API contract documentation, versioning and consumer notification for the new endpoint on api-gateway affecting mobile-banking, and retain the review evidence.
Confirm operational monitoring, alerting and release evidence for the changed components is captured in the change record before deployment.
